in the rows marked as `Hyperbolic' (corresponding to the cost $\ell^2$), we used $\tau_{TTP'}^\theta$
the total tumor size exceeds the progression threshold
can be a nearly-optimal strategy for the long-term management of the disease

issues.failure_explanation: The introduction says the hyperbolic-cost policy outperforms MTD and AT on average in TTP. Table Sum_Hyp contradicts this for n0=0.25: the mean is 102 days versus 210 for MTD and 213 for AT. For n0=0.5 and 0.75 the policy is scored with the modified metric TTP', which ignores the early excursion above the progression threshold, while the benchmarks are scored with TTP. Under the paper's own TTP definition the policy progresses early. The later 'nearly-optimal' claim rests on a nonconvex gradient-descent output and a surrogate cost, not on TTP optimality.

failure_location.quote: on average it outperforms MTD and AT in terms of `time to progression'

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the claim to n0 in {0.5, 0.75} and state that the advantage holds in TTP', not TTP; drop or qualify 'nearly-optimal'.
issues.overall_effect: The headline performance claim for the ensemble-optimal policy is unsupported for one of the three regimes and holds for the others only under a different metric than the benchmarks.
issues.title: Overclaim that the hyperbolic-cost policy outperforms MTD and AT in time to progression
issues.why_classification: The edit is short, but it withdraws a substantive advertised performance claim for part of the regime and changes the metric under which it holds.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: and we can deduce that the set $\Delta_1$ is invariant

issues.failure_explanation: On s=0 we have dr/dt = r(r_R(1-r) - d_T). This changes sign at r = 1 - d_T/r_R, not at r_R/(r_R+d_T). For example, with r_R=1, d_T=0.5 and r=0.6, dr/dt = -0.06 < 0, although the proof claims dr/dt >= 0 there. The case analysis is wrong, and it is undefined when r_R = d_T = 0. Invariance still follows from dr/dt = 0 at r=0 and dr/dt <= 0 at r=1.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the threshold with 1 - d_T/r_R (or argue directly from the endpoint signs at r=0 and r=1).
issues.overall_effect: The proof contains a false computation, but the lemma's conclusion survives, as do lem:extension and the results that use it.
issues.title: Incorrect sign-change threshold on the segment s=0 in the invariance proof
issues.why_classification: A local recomputation fixes the step, and the lemma and its uses are unaffected.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: we divided the interval $[0.002,1]$ into $49$ nodes with a constant step equal to $0.002$
which has a support consisting of $N=1225$ points

issues.failure_explanation: The grid {0.5, 0.52, ..., 1} has 26 nodes, not 25, and {0.002, 0.004, ..., 0.1} has 50 nodes, not 49. With weights 1/25 and 1/49 over the listed grids, mu_N is not a probability measure, and Theta_N has 1300 points, not 1225. Several repairs are possible (different step, dropped endpoint, or corrected counts and weights), and they give different ensembles.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the actual grids and weights used (e.g., 26 and 50 nodes with weights 1/26 and 1/50, N=1300), or correct the step sizes.
issues.overall_effect: The ensemble on which all numerical results are computed is ambiguously defined, which affects reproducibility of the tables.
issues.title: Discrete ensemble measure mu_N is inconsistently specified
issues.why_classification: This is a local specification fix; the method and the qualitative conclusions are unaffected.

issues.failure_explanation: Suppose n touches 1.2 n0 only at tau-bar and then returns below it. Then TTP = tau-bar, but the set {n <= 1.2 n0} contains every later time, so TTP' equals the end of the horizon (or +infinity), not tau-bar. The claim needs n > 1.2 n0 for tau > tau-bar, i.e. a transversal and permanent crossing. The first inequality, TTP <= TTP', also fails on a finite window if the threshold is never reached (TTP = +infinity).

failure_location.quote: If for some $\theta$ there exists a unique instant $\bar \tau >0$ such that

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis that n exceeds 1.2 n0 for all tau > tau-bar, and handle the case where the threshold is never reached.
issues.overall_effect: The stated relation between the two progression metrics is false in degenerate cases; the experimental observations it accompanies are unaffected.
issues.title: Claimed TTP=TTP' under a unique threshold instant fails for tangential contact
issues.why_classification: Adding a standard local hypothesis fixes it, and no other result depends on it.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: tends automatically to find the interval where the decision-making on the therapy schedule has the most significant effect

issues.failure_explanation: By prop:grad_rep the adjoint satisfies g(T)=0, with a uniformly bounded derivative, and F_1 is bounded. Hence the gradient (eq:grad_J) is at most C(T - tau) for every admissible u and every horizon T. Gradients are therefore always small near T, whatever T is, so the 'test' cannot fail. Its interpretation as evidence that late decisions do not matter, and the claim in rmk:choice_T that the method finds the relevant interval automatically, are unsupported.

failure_location.quote: We can use this phenomenon as an empirical test for deciding whether the time horizon $T$ has been appropriately set large

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Withdraw the test and the automatic-interval claim; justify T by sensitivity runs with larger horizons.
issues.overall_effect: The justification for the arbitrary horizon choice in table:Time_horizon is invalid.
issues.title: Small gradient near T is structural, so it cannot test the horizon choice
issues.why_classification: The methodological claim is lost entirely and replacing it needs new experiments, though the main numerical tables are not invalidated.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: as it shows an improvement in almost every performance indicator compared to `Off-On'~AT

issues.failure_explanation: Off-On AT keeps u=0 until n >= 1.2 n0, so by eq:def_TTP progression occurs exactly at the first switch. With d_T=0 and logistic growth, this happens after roughly 9, 15 and 41 days for n0 = 0.25, 0.5 and 0.75, and the threshold is touched again every cycle. The reported Off-On TTPs (107 to 1500 days) therefore cannot be eq:def_TTP; they must use TTP' or another convention, which the paper does not disclose. On-Off AT, which never reaches 1.2 n0 before escape, is scored with TTP. A max of 1500 days, exactly the horizon, also suggests censoring. The claimed superiority of Off-On AT rests on inconsistent metrics, and under the paper's own TTP definition it is far worse.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must re-evaluate all strategies with one consistent progression metric (and an uncensored horizon), then restate whether any advantage of Off-On AT survives.
issues.overall_effect: The paper's proposed contribution, that Off-On AT shows promising improvement over On-Off AT, is unsupported as reported.
issues.title: Off-On AT reaches the progression threshold by design, so its reported TTPs contradict the TTP definition
issues.why_classification: The central advertised advantage of the new strategy may vanish or reverse under consistent evaluation, and no repair within the source preserves it.
